chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Church music, Methodist and Baptist, and a daughter who is a nun
summary: Collins played banjo in church, is a Catholic convert, recalls a moving a cappella spiritual by a Montgomery minister, and his nun daughter attended his concert.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Yeah, well I've played for church, you know, played banjo in church. You know. I'm well versed in --

But I'm a convert. But I was a Methodist. My grandmother played for the Baptist church, and my mother at one time played for the Methodist church. So I couldn't escape, you know. It was fire and brimstone all the way, all along the line, you know. So --
Did the Methodists have as much music as the Baptists?
Yeah. There's a lot of music in the

Methodist church too. I was in Montgomery, a couple of summers ago I had some illness in my family there. And I went to the church where I had attended as a kid, that my mother had played, and there were people who remembered me. And I had such beautiful memories of sitting in this balcony, and it's, you know. And they had a minister -- why I'm telling you this is they had a minister there, who preached a marvelous sermon, but then he sang. He sang spirituals and it just thrilled me. I got chills up and down my spine, you know. A young minister a Capella and he just cold, archipelago, he started, just started singing. But this is the Methodist and the Baptist religion, this is the way they are down south particularly.
But I'm now a Catholic, and as a matter of fact as you know I have a daughter who's a nun, who is also a very fine guitarist. Yes, she's a very fine guitarist. (Jan. Nothing but classics.)
How does she feel about that?
Loves it. Loves it. I did a concert Sunday and she was right down front, sitting there admiring a daddy.

Yeah, I did a concert this past Sunday and in my group I had Jimmy Jones, piano, Harold Jones, drums, and Jim Hewitt, bass. Just quartet. And it was quite nice, I enjoyed it very much. But my daughter was there, you know.
